title: Principal kernel of a Cohen monoid presentation with full boundary image
statement:
Let $C$ be a Cohen ring with residue field $k$ of prime characteristic $p$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring], let $P$ be a fine saturated sharp additive monoid [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], and let $n\ge0$. Sharp means that $0$ is its only invertible element, and put $r=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbf Z}P^{m gp}$. Write $C[P][T_1,\ldots,T_n]$ for the finite-sum ring with monomials $z^qT^e$ and $z^qz^{q'}=z^{q+q'}$, and let $B$ be its completion at $(p,z^q\ (q
e0),T_1,\ldots,T_n)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Put $J=(z^q\ (q
e0),T_1,\ldots,T_n)B$. Let $(S,\mathfrak m_S)$ be a nonzero Noetherian local commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] of finite Krull dimension $n+r$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], and let $\phi:B	woheadrightarrow S$ be a surjective local ring homomorphism satisfying $\phi(J)=\mathfrak m_S$. Then there exists $j\in J$ with $\phi(j)=\phi(p)$. For every such $j$, put $	heta=p-j$. One has $	heta-p\in J$ and $\ker\phi=(	heta)$, and the induced map $B/(	heta)\xrightarrow{\sim}S$ is an isomorphism of local rings taking the classes of $z^q,T_i$ to $\phi(z^q),\phi(T_i)$. More precisely, for $N=(z^q:q
e0)B$ the canonical quotient $B/N\cong D=C[[T_1,\ldots,T_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] carries $	heta$ to $\overline	heta\equiv p\pmod{(T_1,\ldots,T_n)}$, with $\overline	heta\in\mathfrak m_D\setminus\mathfrak m_D^2$, where $\mathfrak m_D=(p,T_1,\ldots,T_n)D$. The ring $B/(	heta)$ is a Noetherian local integral domain of dimension $n+r$. No completeness, log structure or presentation of $S$ is assumed. The cases $P=\{0\}$ and $n=0$ are allowed.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(ii), printed p. 70, the relation congruent to p modulo the monomials and parameters; agent refinement of the principal-kernel argument, extracted from old completed-chart Step 5 together with its invocation of the Step 4 prime-chain argument. Model dimension and normality are the existing separate lem-trf-formal-monoid-ring-dimension and lem-trf-log-regular-saturation-normality, not new claims to duplicate.

proof.text: Put $D=C[[T_1,\ldots,T_n]]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete], $D$ is nonzero complete regular Noetherian local of dimension $n+1$, with maximal ideal $(p,T_1,\ldots,T_n)$. The comparison [lem-trf-polynomial-power-series-monoid-completion] identifies $B$ with the completed monoid ring $H$ over $D$, fixing coefficients, monomials and variables, and identifies $B/N$ canonically with $D$. Apply [lem-trf-formal-monoid-ring-dimension] to $D,P$: $B$ is a Noetherian local domain of dimension $n+1+r$.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(ii), printed p. 70; agent-supplied principal-kernel argument using the existing dimension and normality inputs.

proof.text: The element $p$ is a nonunit in $B$: its image under $B\to D$ is in $\mathfrak m_D$, whereas homomorphisms preserve units. Since $B$ is local, $p$ lies in its maximal ideal; since $\phi$ is local, $\phi(p)\in\mathfrak m_S=\phi(J)$. Choose $j\in J$ with $\phi(j)=\phi(p)$. Fix any such $j$ and put $\theta=p-j$. Then $\phi(\theta)=0$ and $\theta-p=-j\in J$. Under $B/N=D$, the generators of $N$ vanish and the $T_i$ remain $T_i$, so $\overline j\in(T_1,\ldots,T_n)D$ and $\overline\theta\equiv p$ modulo this ideal.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(ii), printed p. 70; agent-supplied principal-kernel argument using the existing dimension and normality inputs.

proof.text: The constant-coefficient homomorphism $D\to C$ sends $\mathfrak m_D$ into $pC$ and sends $\overline\theta$ to $p$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Therefore $\overline\theta\in\mathfrak m_D$ and membership in $\mathfrak m_D^2$ would imply $p\in p^2C$. This is impossible: $C$ is a domain, $p\ne0$, and $p$ is a nonunit [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring]; cancellation in $p=p^2c$ would make $p$ a unit. Hence $\overline\theta\in\mathfrak m_D\setminus\mathfrak m_D^2$.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(ii), printed p. 70; agent-supplied principal-kernel argument using the existing dimension and normality inputs.

proof.text: Apply the primitive-element clause of [lem-trf-formal-monoid-ring-dimension] to $\theta$ under the comparison of Step 1. It gives $\dim Q=(n+1)+r-1=n+r$ for $Q=B/(\theta)$. Since $P$ is fine saturated sharp and $\theta-p\in J$, case (ii) of [lem-trf-log-regular-saturation-normality] says that $Q$ is a nonzero integral domain. As a quotient of the Noetherian local ring $B$ by an ideal in its maximal ideal, $Q$ is Noetherian local: ideals pull back to finitely generated ideals, and its maximal ideals correspond to those of $B$ containing $(\theta)$.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(ii), printed p. 70; agent-supplied principal-kernel argument using the existing dimension and normality inputs.

proof.text: Because $\theta\in\ker\phi$, $\phi$ induces a surjection $\psi:Q\to S$. Write $K=\ker\psi$ and $d=n+r$. If $K\ne0$, take a prime chain $\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_d$ in $S$; such a chain exists because its dimension is the finite integer $d$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Its inverse images in $Q$ are prime (test products under $\psi$), distinct (use surjectivity), and all contain $K$. Their first member is nonzero. Since $Q$ is a domain, $(0)$ is prime, and prepending it gives a chain of length $d+1$ in $Q$, contradicting $\dim Q=d$. Thus $K=0$, and pulling back to $B$ gives $\ker\phi=(\theta)$.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(ii), printed p. 70; agent-supplied principal-kernel argument using the existing dimension and normality inputs.

proof.text: The induced map $\psi:B/(\theta)\to S$ is now bijective, hence a ring isomorphism; it carries every indicated generator class to its image under $\phi$ by its defining formula. An isomorphism preserves units in both directions, so it identifies the unique maximal ideals and is an isomorphism of local rings. The choice of $j$ was arbitrary throughout. Empty generators cause no change: for $P=\{0\}$ one has $N=0$; for $n=0$ the constant-coefficient map is the identity on $C$. When both vanish, $J=0$, $\theta=p$, and the argument gives $S\cong C/(p)$, a domain of dimension $0$.
